deviations: Pairing law (phase doc §2.1 anticipated; documented in ReplayInputs.kt): the phase-3 transcripts under fixtures/transcripts/ are provider request/response pairs, not per-dump recordings — their state text is the Phase-0 placeholder format and their answer distributions cover only their own 4-option question sets, so a verbatim replay against a real dump's full candidate list would violate the exact name-keyed distribution law (vision 02 §2). Tier A therefore records each dump's gold decision as reviewable DATA (core/src/test/resources/eval/replay-pairings.json: goal + chosen node id + optional explicit actionKind + provenance note) and synthesizes the recorded response deterministically (0.5 on the gold, remainder halving across the other candidates in declared order — pairwise-distinct masses summing to exactly 1.0), then re-parses that body through the REAL wire parser (SystemOneClient.parseAnswers), so state build, question forms, wire parse, and gate classify all run the production code path. Adversarial SUBMIT golds record actionKind explicitly (the tap-vs-submit trap is app-side per Phase 6).

EvalReport carries additive gate-evidence fields (rotationMatrix, rotationStable, selfCheckMutations, selfCheckAllCaught, stateFormatVersion) alongside the phase doc's five named constructor fields (fixtures, outcomes, tokenCounts, bucketStats, timestamp) — Gate 7.3 requires the report to list per-fixture rotation matrix sizes and Gate 7.2's self-check result is carried as standing evidence in the committed artifact.

Gate 7.2's literal 'perturb one bucket's ordering in a scratch copy' is implemented as a bucket-membership perturbation (one candidate dropped from a scratch candidate list while the ORIGINAL recorded response is replayed): pure re-ordering cannot and must not change any outcome (that inversion is exactly Gate 7.3's 100%-stability law), so the catchable injected regression is the membership change — the recorded distribution then carries a key outside the declared option ids and the wire parser fails loudly, naming the dropped candidate; the harness probe records the fixture. Two further probes (shifted recorded response, deliberately positional resolver under rotation) prove the expectation comparison and the rotation check have no false green.

Run timestamp is caller-supplied metadata written verbatim into the artifacts (default = wall clock; the Gradle run for the committed artifacts pinned 2026-10-03T19:24:43.2518562Z): determinism is defined over report content — the determinism test compares two runs at a fixed timestamp and the drift detector regenerates with the committed artifact's pinned timestamp, so committed bytes stay stable until a reviewed code change moves them.
